claim_text: Steam had a broad outage on Tuesday evening, Nov 17, that took down online features
summary: On Nov 17, Steam downloads, the Friends list, cloud saves and the Store were unreachable for many users, with 'No Connection' errors. XDA's writer says he saw it first-hand.
detail: XDA says it could not download games, its Friends list was gone, cloud saves would not load and the store was limited. IT Home reports the same features down and says third-party monitors showed Steam services dropping sharply. Instatus's tracker page shows a spike starting about 5 PM ET (10 PM UTC) and no incident posted by Steam.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: XDA's first-hand check, an independent outlet (IT Home), and an independent tracker agree on the outage.
notes: IBTimes AU repeats XDA's account, so it is not counted as a separate source.

claim_text: Downdetector logged more than 30,000 reports, nearly 48,000 at one point, during the Nov 17 outage
summary: XDA reports 'over 30,000' Downdetector reports and 'just under 48,000' at the time of writing. IT Home gives about 48,000 citing foreign media.
detail: These are user-submitted reports, not a count of affected users. We did not read Downdetector itself. IT Home and IBTimes AU rely on XDA's figures. Instatus's own figure for the same night differed between two times we loaded the page, so we do not quote it.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: XDA relays Downdetector's count; the other outlets repeat it.

claim_text: Services came back at about 6:35 PM ET on Nov 17
summary: XDA's update, stamped 6:35 PM EST, says Steam was back online, Downdetector reports were 'in freefall', and all services appeared restored. IBTimes AU repeats this.
detail: Single source for the time. IT Home (written Nov 18) says services had been recovering. Trackers reported by other sites put the downtime from 53 minutes to about an hour.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: The restoration time rests on XDA's update; IT Home only says recovery had begun.

claim_text: The cause of the Nov 17 and Nov 20-21 disruptions
summary: Valve has not said what caused either disruption. We found no Steam status page or post explaining them.
detail: XDA, IT Home, IBTimes AU and Sunday Guardian each say Valve had not given a cause. Instatus lists no Steam incident for Nov 17.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: Four outlets report that Valve gave no cause.

claim_text: The Nov 17 outage was reported as maintenance, which Valve usually runs on Tuesday evenings
summary: XDA's headline and text say Steam was 'down for maintenance' based on what people were reporting, and note Valve usually runs maintenance around 3-6 PM Pacific. IBTimes AU says the same about users' description.
detail: XDA's own text says 'people are reporting' maintenance and that this one ran longer than usual. IT Home says Valve had not said whether it was maintenance. We did not find a Valve notice of maintenance.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: The maintenance claim is XDA's reading of user reports; no Valve statement backs it.

claim_text: Late Friday night, Nov 20, users reported sign-in and connection failures starting about 11:47 PM ET
summary: IBTimes AU, citing the tracker IsItDownRightNow, says reports jumped from about 11:47 PM ET, topping 1,600 in an hour against about 62 at the same time on a normal day. Users described sign-in failures and an 'E502 L2' error.
detail: The numbers come from automated user-report trackers, which IBTimes AU says show complaints, not confirmed failures. We did not open IsItDownRightNow or StatusGator ourselves. The disruption looked ongoing into early Saturday.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: One outlet relays the trackers' figures and user descriptions.

claim_text: On Saturday, Nov 21, users reported checkout and purchase errors; Downdetector showed 1,042 reports against a baseline of 14
summary: Sunday Guardian Live says a Downdetector snapshot it timed at 9:27 AM showed 1,042 reports against a usual 14 (about 74 times normal), with failed purchases and an 'E502 L2' message. It says this is not a platform-wide shutdown.
detail: The article does not state the time zone of its 9:27 AM snapshot, and its own header is stamped earlier than that time in India. Treat the clock time as unclear. The 'E502 L2' error also appears in IBTimes AU's account of Friday night.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Sunday Guardian relays a Downdetector snapshot and user messages; the error code matches IBTimes AU's.

claim_text: Independent monitoring showed Steam's sites still reachable during the Friday-Saturday reports
summary: IBTimes AU says some services that test Steam's public websites showed them reachable during parts of Friday night. Sunday Guardian says independent checks showed Store, Community and Client responding normally on Nov 21.
detail: This suggests the problems hit some features or users more than others. Neither outlet names the monitors in a way we could check, and we did not run any checks ourselves.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Two outlets say the same, but both are describing monitors we did not read.

claim_text: The Friday-Saturday spike fell outside Valve's usual Tuesday maintenance window
summary: IBTimes AU says Steam usually does routine maintenance on Tuesday evenings US time and that Friday night's spike came outside that schedule.
detail: Valve has not published its maintenance schedule in any source we read; this is the outlet's description of a usual pattern.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: One outlet's statement about the usual schedule.

claim_text: Valve had not commented on the Friday-Saturday reports
summary: IBTimes AU says Valve had not commented or confirmed an outage when it was written. Sunday Guardian says there was no verified official confirmation of a cause.
detail: We found no Steam status page or Valve post on these reports. Valve may have said something after those articles were written.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Two outlets report Valve's silence as of their writing.

claim_text: No source we read says either Steam disruption was a cyberattack, or rules one out
summary: We found no claim of responsibility, no report of an attack and no Valve statement on cause. We also found no statement ruling an attack out. Tracker spikes are not evidence of an attack.
detail: A search for a DDoS claim or hack report about Steam in Nov 2026 found none. One Romanian outlet (not cited here) said it is not right to blame a cyberattack, a server fault or a network problem without confirmation; we did not read it in full.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: None of the sources gives a cause or mentions an attack.

claim_text: The Nov 17 and Nov 20-21 disruptions are connected, or are part of this month's other outages
summary: No source links the two Steam disruptions to each other or to the FAA, Microsoft 365, Ticketmaster or other outages of recent weeks.
detail: IBTimes AU says it is not clear whether Friday night's problems relate to Tuesday's maintenance outage.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: No source ties these events together.

claim_text: The White House said on Nov 18 it sees no indication of a cyberattack behind recent tech outages; it did not name Steam
summary: A Nov 18 White House release quotes the DNI and the National Security Adviser saying they see no indication of a coordinated cyberattack and no evidence the recent incidents are related.
detail: The release came a day after the Nov 17 Steam outage and before the Nov 20-21 reports, and does not mention Steam or Valve. It is context, not a finding about Steam.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The release is the primary source for what officials said.
